title: Cosmo-tomography toward PKS 1830‒211: Variability of the quasar and of its foreground molecular absorption monitored with ALMA
question: How do the submillimeter continuum emission and foreground molecular absorption of the lensed quasar PKS 1830-211 vary over time, and what constraints do these variations place on the quasar's activity and small-scale ISM structures in the z=0.89 absorber?

data.sensitivity: 0.47% to 2.14% of SW continuum per 0.6 km/s channel (individual visits); < 0.1%-0.2% (2016 averaged spectrum); 0.1% to 1.3% (complementary spectra)

evidence.quote: To these water spectra, we can add the observations of the CH$^+$ (1-0) line in 2015 (reported by (cite: mul17)).
For H$_2$O, the frequency is taken from (cite: caz09).

what.value: Rest frequencies and relative intensities of CH

evidence.quote: For CH, frequencies are taken from (cite: tru14) and line relative intensities ($S_{ul}$) from (cite: nij12).
For $^{13}$CH, spectroscopic data are taken from (cite: hal08) and the JPL molecular spectroscopy database.

(cite: she08) derive a quasi-linear relationship between the column densities of CH and H$_2$, with an average abundance ratio of [CH]/[H$_2$] $= 3.5 _{-1.4}^{+2.1} \times 10^{-8}$ along diffuse molecular sightlines and dark clouds.
For water, (cite: fla13) also find a remarkably constant abundance ratio relative to H$_2$ in Galactic translucent clouds, with [H$_2$O]/[H$_2$] $= (4.8 \pm 0.3) \times 10^{-8}$.

recipe.goal: Extract continuum flux densities, flux-density ratios, differential polarimetry, and absorption spectra from calibrated visibilities
recipe.method: Visibility fitting with a two point-source model in UVMultiFit on Stokes I, XX, and YY separately; extraction of spectral indices after flagging absorption channels
key_parameters: Two point-like components; free parameters: f_NE and R = f_NE/f_SW
assumptions: Third lensed image and small Einstein ring extensions are negligible and ignored

recipe.goal: Estimate time delay and differential magnification via randomness minimization
recipe.method: Measure-of-randomness analysis on the combined NE and time-shifted, scaled SW light curves using the Von Neumann estimator
key_parameters: Grid over time delay Delta t and differential magnification R_q
assumptions: Minimum randomness corresponds to the most likely values of Delta t and R_q

recipe.goal: Model continuum light curve, spectral index evolution, and polarization with a core + ballistic plasmon model
recipe.method: Simultaneous parametric fit to NE/SW flux densities, NE spectral index, and spectral-index difference using MCMC; qualitative extension to Stokes Q polarization
key_parameters: Plasmon injection time t_0, core flux I_c (< 0.18 Jy), plasmon flux I_p, decay power beta, plasmon spectral index alpha_p, time delay Delta t, differential magnification R_q; for polarization exploration: Gaussian F(t-t0) with width 100 days, m_c = 0.05, m_p = 0.2
assumptions: No micro- or milli-lensing; stable optically thick core (alpha_c = 0, I_c < 0.18 Jy); single ballistic plasmon injection; adiabatic losses dominate over radiative losses; electron energy index p = 3

recipe.goal: Characterize absorption line variability using Principal Component Analysis (PCA)
recipe.method: PCA decomposition of monitoring absorption spectra to extract eigenspectra and time-evolving eigenvalues, followed by sinusoidal fitting to eigenvalue time series
key_parameters: Velocity intervals: SW H2O [-100, 100], [-100, 0], [0, 100] km/s; SW CH1 and CH2 [-60, 60] km/s; NE H2O [-240, -120] km/s
assumptions: All eigenvalues taken with equal weight in sine function fit

recipe.goal: Construct deep averaged 2016 spectra and measure 12CH/13CH ratio
recipe.method: Remove first-order polynomial baseline from each visit's spectrum, compute inverse-variance weighted average, and simultaneously fit multi-Gaussian velocity components convolved with hyperfine structure to 12CH and 13CH doublets
assumptions: Same intrinsic velocity profile for 12CH and 13CH; optically thin lines; no chemical fractionation

recipe.goal: Derive water isotopolog and oxygen isotopic ratios (16O/18O and 18O/17O)
recipe.method: Simultaneous multi-Gaussian opacity profile fitting to H2(16)O, H2(18)O, H2(17)O, and CH spectra from 2014 and 2022 epochs, then combining with statistical weights
key_parameters: N_gauss = 3, 5, or 9 Gaussian components; continuum covering factor f_c free (when H2(16)O included) or fixed to 1
assumptions: Same opacity velocity profile for all isotopologs and CH; no fractionation for water isotopologs

recipe.goal: Deconvolve CH hyperfine structure and correlate H2O and CH optical depths
recipe.method: Convert absorption profiles to optical depth assuming f_c = 1, deconvolve CH hyperfine structure using a Clean algorithm, and compare tau(H2O) with tau(CH*)
key_parameters: f_c = 1; T_CMB = 5.14 K at z = 0.89; H2O ortho-to-para ratio = 3
assumptions: f_c = 1 (excluding saturated [-10, +10] km/s center); hfs intensities follow statistical weights; LTE with CMB at 5.14 K; H2O OPR = 3

answer_key.quantity: NE image continuum flux density drop (2016 monitoring)

evidence.quote: In contrast to the large decrease in flux density during the 2016 monitoring, the instantaneous flux-density ratios $\Re = f_{\rm NE}/f_{\rm SW}$ show only mild ($\sim 10$%) variations around an average value of $\sim 1.04$, with extreme values of 0.96 and 1.15 (Fig. 1 b).
Taken at face value, the average value of all the ALMA flux-density ratios measured between 2012 and 2022 is $1.38 \pm 0.35$ (with 1$\sigma$ dispersion) and the median is 1.29.

evidence.quote: All these measurements (Table 1; except overlapping velocity range for measurements from H$_2$O spectra) are independent, but still yield a consistent signal period of $\sim 230$ days for PC1, within error bars.
Our final $^{12}$CH/$^{13}$CH ratio is $150 \pm 10$.
We also measure the oxygen isotopic ratios, $^{16}$O/$^{18}$O $= 65.3 \pm 0.7$ and $^{18}$O/$^{17}$O $= 11.5 \pm 0.5$ in the $z=0.89$ absorber.

evidence.loc: Water isotopologs and oxygen isotopic ratios
evidence.quote: The values of the $^{16}$O/$^{18}$O ($= 65.3 \pm 0.7$ after combining the measurements with their statistical weights) and $^{18}$O/$^{17}$O ($= 11.5 \pm 0.5$) ratios are consistent with the previous measurements made from the HCO$^+$ isotopologs by (cite: mul06; mul11), albeit with much better accuracy.
We also measure the oxygen isotopic ratios, $^{16}$O/$^{18}$O $= 65.3 \pm 0.7$ and $^{18}$O/$^{17}$O $= 11.5 \pm 0.5$ in the $z=0.89$ absorber.

score_reason: All ALMA project codes, calibration settings (CASA 4.7.2, 10s phase self-cal, calibrators), visibility fitting tool (UVMultiFit), PCA tool (scikit-learn), spectroscopic constants (Table A.1), and per-visit intermediate measurements (Table 1) are explicitly provided; only minor fitting priors and channel masks are omitted.
rediscovery_reason: All six ALMA datasets are public, visibility modeling with UVMultiFit is straightforward for two point sources, and the main results (flux ratios, PCA periods, 12CH/13CH = 150 +/- 10, 16O/18O = 65.3 +/- 0.7, 18O/17O = 11.5 +/- 0.5, and time delay 25 +/- 3 days) are crisp numeric targets.
